card.name: Comma after a serious adverse event
card.fires_on: The comma right after a named serious adverse event such as pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity or hepatic injury in warning text. It comes just before a qualifier like "including fatal cases" or "some severe".

modes.label: Comma after condition name
modes.description: Comma straight after a condition name in a warnings heading or first sentence, before "including fatal...".
modes.example: 5.2 Pancreatitis There have been postmarketing reports of acute pancreatitis<<,>> including fatal and non-fatal hemorrhagic

modes.label: Comma after "have been reported"
modes.description: Comma after a list of reported liver problems, before "some of which".
modes.example: Hepatotoxicity Abnormal liver function, hepatitis, cholestatic jaundice, hepatic necrosis, and hepatic failure have been reported<<,>> some of which have resulted in death.

card.writes: It promotes words meaning "sometimes" or "some", which fits a qualifier about only some cases being severe or fatal.
card.plain: It fires on the comma after a serious side effect, where the text goes on to say that some cases were severe or fatal.
